title: What's New in Micetro 26.2
prompt:
Product: BlueCat. Demo: "What's New in Micetro 26.2".
Start with one welcome step whose title is exactly "What's New in Micetro 26.2" and whose text is exactly: Google Cloud, network discovery, API keys and a dark theme, plus the new MCP server for AI assistants, in about three minutes.
Audience: network and DNS engineers and IT leaders evaluating the product. Tone: concise, confident, practical, no hype.
7 screenshots, keep this order, one tooltip per image, calling out the highlighted UI element. Use the text of each numbered tooltip EXACTLY as written; do not rewrite, shorten or merge it. Do not add a closing step or a closing message after the last screenshot; its own tooltip is the end.
1. Micetro 26.2 is here. Four changes to see, plus the new MCP server for AI assistants, starting with Google Cloud.
2. Google Cloud joins AWS and Azure. Add a project as a service and its Cloud DNS zones sit in the same list as every other zone. Next, discovery.
3. Discovery now collects IPv6 as well as IPv4, and it writes only into the organization that owns the SNMP profile. Next, API keys.
4. Automation gets a user and a key of its own, limited to a read-only role, instead of borrowing a person's account. Here the key reads DNS zones. Next, the interface.
5. Pick light or dark, or follow your system setting. It is a personal preference, so each person chooses their own. Next, an AI assistant.
6. Also new: an AI assistant can work from your real DNS and DHCP data. Here it spots a default gateway on the wrong subnet. The MCP server is read-only, so it can look but not change. Last, the smaller changes in 26.2.
7. There is more in 26.2: a request limit for AWS, Meraki China support, tidier DHCP files, and new Ansible and Terraform releases. Pick the one new feature that matches your biggest pain, and try it first.
